lines.text: Jehu wrote to the officials in Samaria, and terrified, they answered that they would not make anyone king.
Jehu's second letter demanded the heads of Ahab's sons at Samaria, and Jehu ordered them piled at the gate.
Jehu said the LORD acted through His servant Isaiah, and he killed everyone left of Ahab's house in Jezreel.
At Beth-eked, Jehu met relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah, and his men slaughtered forty-two of them at the well.
Jehu took Jehonadab into his chariot to see his zeal for the LORD, then struck down Ahab's people in Samaria.
